# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb report. Display reads 0. There is a light, currently yellow. Five wires in order: wire 1 white, wire 2 red, wire 3 yellow, wire 4 green, wire 5 blue. Mute, check the manual for these colors and the yellow light. Blind, that is the layout you will be feeling.

Deaf has given me the full layout: display 0, light yellow, wires 1-5 = white, red, yellow, green, blue. I can't verify any of this myself — I only know what my hands feel, and I haven't touched anything yet. But this is the layout I'll be working with. I have no manual knowledge, so I don't yet know which wire to cut. Mute needs to read the manual and tell us the rule. I should acknowledge to Mute that I've received the layout and am ready to act once they give the instruction. I'll speak to Mute (my only voice channel) and gesture to Deaf/Mute to confirm.

Actually, let me think about what's useful. I have nothing new to add — Deaf already reported the layout. Mute is the one who must now consult the manual. I can simply confirm readiness. Since I speak to Mute only, and gesture to Deaf+Mute, I'll send a short confirmation.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Layout received: display 0, yellow light, wires white red yellow green blue. I can reach the wires and cut any position 1-5. Waiting on your manual reading for which wire to cut.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: Mute sent me a gesture I cannot yet interpret, and you cannot see it. It was five fists then a thumbs up. I am asking Mute to clarify. Also, did your thumbs up mean you understood my bomb description?

Deaf is asking me a direct question: did my thumbs up mean I understood the bomb description? Yes, it did. Also, Deaf reports Mute sent a gesture I can't see: five fists then a thumbs up. Five fists — that could mean "cut wire 5"? Or it could mean something else. A fist is ✊. Five fists then 👍. Hmm, that's ambiguous. I can't see gestures anyway; Deaf is relaying it.

I should answer Deaf's question clearly. But I can only gesture to Deaf (gestures go to Deaf and Mute), and speak to Mute. I can't speak to Deaf. So to answer Deaf, I must gesture. A 👍 would confirm. But I also want to help interpret Mute's gesture.

Five fists then thumbs up — if each fist represents a wire position, five fists = wire 5? Or "fists" might be counting. Actually Mute can't speak, only gesture or read manual. Mute is trying to communicate the manual's instruction via gesture. Five fists then 👍 could mean "cut wire 5" — but that's a guess.

I should confirm to Deaf via gesture, and ask Mute via speech to clarify the instruction in words (since Mute can hear me speak, and Mute can't speak but... wait, Mute can't speak and can't gesture? No — Mute "cannot speak, or touch the bomb." Mute CAN gesture. Mute reads the manual. Mute's output is gestures only.)

Wait, can Mute write? No, speech is a voice. Mute cannot speak. So Mute communicates only by gesture. That's a problem — gestures only reach Deaf and me (Blind) as... no, I never receive gesture. Deaf receives gestures. So Mute's manual knowledge reaches me only through Deaf relaying it.

So the chain: Mute reads manual → gestures to Deaf → Deaf speaks to me (Blind) the interpretation. And I speak to Mute.

So I need Deaf to interpret Mute's gesture. Five fists + thumbs up. Let me think: maybe Mute is counting wires and indicating the fifth. Or Mute means "cut wire 5." I should ask Mute directly in speech to confirm: "Do you mean cut wire 5?"

Let me gesture 👍 to Deaf (confirming understanding) and speak to Mute asking for clarification.

Actually, I should be careful. Let me just confirm to Deaf and ask Mute to clarify in a way that reaches me. But Mute can't speak to me — Mute can only gesture, which I can't see. So the only way Mute's answer reaches me is via Deaf. So I should ask Deaf to relay, and ask Mute to gesture clearly.

Let me send: gesture 👍 to Deaf (yes, understood). Speak to Mute: "Deaf relayed your gesture as five fists then thumbs up. I can't see gestures. Please repeat clearly so Deaf can interpret — do you mean cut wire 5?"

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot see gestures. Deaf relayed yours as five fists then a thumbs up. If that means cut wire 5, please gesture it again clearly so Deaf can confirm the interpretation. I can cut any position 1-5 on your word.")
```

Deaf says to Blind: Still waiting on the manual rule from Mute. Your thumbs up is received and understood as yes. I will relay the rule to you as soon as Mute gives it.

Deaf confirms my thumbs up was understood, and is still waiting on Mute's manual rule. There's nothing new for me to act on yet. I have no independent information — I can't see the bomb and I can't read the manual. My only job is to wait for the rule, then cut the correct wire.

I should be patient. No need to send noise. But I could gently prompt Mute again since the manual rule is the critical missing piece. However, I already asked. Sending another message risks cluttering. Still, Mute may be stuck on how to convey the rule via gestures. Let me offer a useful suggestion: Mute could gesture the wire number as a count (fingers), and confirm with thumbs up/down. That might help Mute communicate.

Actually, a helpful move: tell Mute the encoding I can work with via Deaf. Since Mute hears me, I can propose a clear code: "gesture the number of fingers equal to the wire position to cut." That gives Mute a simple, unambiguous channel.

Let me speak to Mute proposing this encoding, and gesture to Deaf to relay that I'm proposing an encoding.

```
speak(to="mute", text="To make the rule clear through Deaf: gesture the wire position as that many fingers (one finger = wire 1, five fingers = wire 5), then a thumbs up to confirm cut. If the manual says something else, gesture it and Deaf will relay. I will wait for your signal.")

```
